title: Tracking glacier retreat with multi-decade satellite imagery
abstract: We combine 38 years of Landsat imagery with a convolutional segmentation model to map terminus positions for 412 marine-terminating glaciers in Greenland. Retreat accelerated after 2000 in 71% of glaciers, with the strongest signal in the southeast. We release the annotated terminus dataset and the trained model.

title: A graph neural network for predicting crystal formation energy
abstract: We train a message-passing graph neural network on 140,000 DFT-computed inorganic crystals to predict formation energy. The model reaches a mean absolute error of 0.031 eV/atom on a held-out test set and screens 2.1 million hypothetical compounds in under four GPU-hours, identifying 312 candidate stable phases for experimental follow-up.

title: Single-cell atlas of the developing zebrafish retina
abstract: Using single-cell RNA sequencing of 96,000 cells across nine developmental time points, we construct a transcriptional atlas of the zebrafish retina. Trajectory analysis identifies two previously undescribed progenitor states that precede photoreceptor commitment. All data are available through an interactive browser.

title: Measuring misinformation spread on community forums
abstract: We analyze 4.3 million posts from 1,200 regional community forums between 2019 and 2023. Using a fine-tuned language model to label claims, we find that corrections posted within two hours reduce reshares of false claims by 38%, while later corrections have no measurable effect. We discuss implications for moderation policy.

title: Scaling molecular dynamics to exascale with asynchronous task graphs
abstract: We restructure a classical molecular dynamics code around an asynchronous task graph runtime. On 4,096 GPUs the new design achieves 82% parallel efficiency for a 1.2-billion-atom system, compared with 41% for the bulk-synchronous baseline. Load imbalance from heterogeneous particle density is the main remaining bottleneck.

title: Soil microbiome shifts under cover-crop rotation
abstract: Over a four-year field trial in central Illinois we sampled soil microbial communities under three cover-crop rotations. 16S amplicon sequencing shows that cereal rye rotations increase nitrogen-fixing taxa by 22% relative to fallow controls, and these shifts correlate with a 9% yield increase in the following corn crop.

title: Detecting gravitational-wave transients with a lightweight transformer
abstract: We present a transformer model with 3.4 million parameters that detects binary black hole mergers in strain data from two detectors. At a false-alarm rate of one per month the model recovers 94% of injected signals with network SNR above 8, and processes one hour of data in 1.8 seconds on a single GPU, enabling low-latency alerts.

title: Language models as research assistants: an evaluation of literature triage
abstract: We evaluate five open-weight language models on screening 6,000 biomedical abstracts for a systematic review. The best model achieves 0.91 recall at 0.62 precision against expert labels, reducing human screening workload by 55%. Performance drops sharply for abstracts outside the model's training distribution, motivating human-in-the-loop review.

title: Urban heat islands and emergency room visits
abstract: Linking high-resolution land surface temperature to 2.7 million emergency department visits across 14 US cities, we estimate that each 1 degree C increase in neighborhood surface temperature raises heat-related visits by 6.4%. Effects are largest in census tracts with low tree canopy cover and high proportions of residents over 65.

title: Neural activity during spatial navigation in freely moving mice
abstract: Using a head-mounted miniature microscope we record calcium activity from 1,800 hippocampal neurons while mice explore novel and familiar environments. Place-cell maps stabilize within three sessions in familiar arenas but remain variable in novel arenas, suggesting experience-dependent consolidation of spatial representations.

title: Low-cost sensors for monitoring river nitrate
abstract: We deploy 60 low-cost optical nitrate sensors across an agricultural watershed and calibrate them against laboratory measurements. After calibration, sensor readings agree with laboratory values within 0.4 mg/L. The network reveals short nitrate pulses after storms that monthly grab sampling misses entirely.

title: Automated grading feedback in introductory programming courses
abstract: In a randomized study across 900 students in an introductory programming course, students who received automatically generated hints on failing test cases resubmitted 30% more often and scored 7 points higher on the final exam than students who only saw pass/fail results. Hint quality was rated helpful by 78% of surveyed students.

title: Protein structure prediction for viral surface proteins
abstract: We apply a structure prediction pipeline to 2,300 viral surface glycoproteins lacking experimental structures. Predicted models with high confidence scores agree with subsequently released cryo-EM structures at a median RMSD of 1.3 angstroms. We identify conserved surface pockets that are candidate targets for broadly neutralizing antibodies.

title: Energy use of AI inference on shared research clusters
abstract: We instrument GPU power draw for 52,000 inference jobs on a university research cluster. Median energy per generated token varies 11-fold across job configurations, driven mostly by batch size and GPU utilization. Simple batching guidance in user documentation reduced average energy per token by 34% over one semester.

title: Reconstructing historical weather from ship logbooks
abstract: We transcribe 210,000 handwritten weather observations from 19th-century ship logbooks using a combination of handwriting recognition and volunteer verification. Assimilating these observations into a reanalysis reduces sea-level pressure uncertainty over the 1850s South Pacific by up to 40%.

title: Predicting crop disease from smartphone leaf images
abstract: We collect 48,000 smartphone photos of soybean leaves labeled for six diseases by plant pathologists. A compact vision model fine-tuned on these images reaches 93% accuracy and runs offline on mid-range phones. Field trials with 85 farmers show diagnosis agreement with experts of 89%.
